Phone Interview Transcript (Reported by Lisa Garcia, 2025-08-19):

Hi there, I hope I’m in the right place—this is Lisa Garcia. I was asked to give all the details again just to make sure everything is in the system, so here goes. I called in on Monday, the 19th (I think that's today?), and the person on the phone gave me that claim number, CLM-692408, so I’d have it handy. They said it helps keep track, in case I get different agents—or if you’re all busy when I call back. Anyway.

So, this happened Sunday evening. I remember that because we were on our way back from my sister’s, and my husband William, whose name should be on the actual policy—I think his number is POL-575631637, but I always get that mixed up—was the one driving our blue 2017 Ford Escape. That’s the one with the little chip in the back left window? We got it valued last year on March 7th (at $16,433) on the same day we got the policy. The policy should run out next year on the 6th.

We were just turning onto Birchwood Lane in our neighborhood; it’s generally quiet except when the local kids are out riding bikes—and, of course, that wasn’t even the issue. We had stopped, my husband was letting a group of ducks cross the street, of all things, when this guy in a silver sedan just slammed right into the back of us. It wasn’t super fast but definitely enough to feel the jolt and hear the crunch. The man got out right away and apologized a bunch—he seemed more rattled than we were.

We actually waited for the police, and while we stood around, someone from down the street brought us lemonade (nice, but not really relevant, I guess). Anyway, the police came—took their time getting the report done, and gave us the paper with PR-20250817-9170 scribbled across the top. We’ve got a copy if anyone needs it again.

I’m reporting this now, two days after it happened—today's the 19th, right?—because we spent Monday morning calling around trying to figure out where we take the car for the estimates. The repair shop said it’ll be about $2,776. That’s just to fix the back bumper and trunk area; thankfully, it’s driveable, so we’ve just been careful about popping it open. I should add, our policy (effective since March of last year) should cover this, I think, but you all can check. It’s the auto policy, not the home, and we haven’t had any accidents before.

So, yeah, sorry if this is too much, but better to have all the details than not enough, right? Oh, and William’s insurance stuff is all bundled with our home, so if you see weird cross-references, that’s why.

Call transcript [System log: 2025-09-10]

Representative: 'Good afternoon, could I have your claim reference?'

Caller: 'Oh right, I was told it’s CLM-741209—I think I wrote it on the back of an envelope somewhere, but yeah, that should be the one.'

---

So, my name is Karen Wilson, and I’m calling about an accident from Monday, September 8th. I honestly still can’t believe it happened. I drive a silver Toyota, the Camry from 2018 (the VIN number ends in …83745, I think—though I always misread that string of digits). I think the car’s still worth around $14,000, at least that’s what the appraisal last year said.' Representative: 'If you'll let me look up your details, I should be able to find that id. Ohh yes, VIN29384756109283745 is covered by the POL-811390245 car insurance policy under your name.' Caller: 'I renewed it last summer, mid-July, on the 15th. I hope it’s still active because, honestly, the last thing I need is a gap in coverage right now.

Anyway, I was stopped at the lights on Main & Fifth when this pickup truck just didn’t stop in time and hit me from behind. It wasn’t massive, but enough that my bumper is a mess and the trunk won’t close properly anymore. I told the officer on scene—he wrote a report, gave me the number: PR-20250908-1289, I think? Something like that. He said it should help when I call this in.

I already got a rough repair estimate from the shop my brother uses—it came to about $4,800 and change, though the mechanic said it could go higher if they find frame issues once they pull the panels off. I don’t remember the exact cents, $4,821 maybe, but I know it was more than I expected.

I mentioned all this to the tow truck guy and he said he’s seen worse. Not helpful! I’m still shaken up, and my daughter keeps asking if we can drive it to school, but it’s not safe until it’s fixed. Also, can someone tell me if rental coverage is part of this policy? I can’t find that page of the paperwork right now.

Sorry for rambling—I know you probably just need the basics, but I figured I’d explain everything in case it matters. Wait, now I'm realizing that the policy was just for one year and expired on the 14th. Am I too late?

text: Around 3:20 in the afternoon on the Gardiner in Toronto. The pavement was still wet from the morning shower. I signalled and started moving over into the middle lane in my silver Honda Civic 2016 and a white pickup that was in my blind spot came up at the same moment and we sideswiped each other. Both of us say the other one should have looked, to be honest I think we share it, I did not check my mirror twice and he was speeding up. Dents and scratched paint down the whole driver side, the mirror hangs by its cable.

text: This is the third time I am writing and nobody answers. Last Saturday at 11:10 at night, in the middle of a heavy rain, I was crossing the intersection at Aurora and 85th in Seattle on a green light in my green Subaru Outback 2018 when a pickup flew through his red and hit the whole passenger side. He did not even slow down, I have the dashcam and the witness statement of the bus driver who was waiting at the stop. The side of my car is caved in up to the middle pillar, both airbags on that side went off, the wheel is bent out and the car was towed from the scene on a flatbed. I had a concussion and three days in the hospital. הוא עבר באדום, ברור לגמרי. The police report names him as the one who ran the light, so this is entirely his fault and I expect a full repair or a total loss payout without more games, I am not paying for his mistake. Please assign a human adjuster.
